extra.message: The document conversion `profile` path variable (DocumentController.convert, /customers/{id}/documents/{docId}/convert/{profile}) is concatenated into a shell command executed via Runtime.getRuntime().exec(new String[]{"sh","-c",command}). cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: importFrom() fetches an arbitrary user-supplied URL (sourceUrl from StatementController.archive) with RestClient.get().uri(sourceUrl). The only validation is a ^https?:// regex, so the server can be coerced to request internal-only services (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8091/internal/..., cloud metadata). Server-Side Request Forgery.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: accountRef (StatementController.catalogue path variable) is concatenated directly into the XPath expression "//statement[account='" + accountRef + "']". An attacker can break out of the string literal (e.g. ' or '1'='1) to alter the query and enumerate other statement records. XPath injection.

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions ('XPath Injection')

extra.message: writeRegister() builds the output path with Path.of(storage.getRoot(), name) using the untrusted {name} path variable (StatementController.register) and writes CSV content there. No normalization or containment check is performed, so ../ sequences escape the storage root and allow arbitrary file write.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: spoolToBranchTray() resolves base.resolve(tray).resolve(...) where `tray` comes from the client-controlled MERIDIAN_BRANCH_TRAY cookie (StatementController.spool). No containment check means a cookie value containing ../ allows writing the statement bytes outside the branch tray root.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: attributes() does base.resolve(ref) with the untrusted `ref` request parameter (DocumentController.inspect, /customers/{id}/documents/inspect) and reads file attributes without normalize()/containment checking. ../../ paths let an attacker probe file existence, size and directory structure outside the storage root.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: applyTariff() parses the user-supplied `tariff` parameter (AdminFeeScheduleController.tariff) with a default DocumentBuilderFactory that has not disabled DTDs/external entities. External entity expansion enables XXE (local file disclosure and SSRF).

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: applyTariffFromFeed() calls new Yaml().load(in) on an uploaded tariff file (FeeTariffController.apply). SnakeYAML's default constructor allows arbitrary Java type instantiation from the document, enabling insecure deserialization / remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data

extra.message: previewWaiver() evaluates the user-supplied SpEL expression (AdminFeeScheduleController.preview `expression` parameter) with new SpelExpressionParser().parseExpression(expression).getValue(...). An attacker can run arbitrary SpEL (e.g. T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec(...)) leading to remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: render() compiles the user-supplied `wording` request parameter as a FreeMarker template (new Template("notice", wording, configuration).process(...)). This is server-side template injection: an attacker can inject FreeMarker directives (e.g. <#assign ex="freemarker.template.utility.Execute"?new()>${ex("id")}) to execute code.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: search() concatenates the untrusted commonName (the MERIDIAN_DIRECTORY_QUERY cookie, RegionalStaffController.directory) into the LDAP filter "(&(objectClass=person)(cn=" + commonName + "))". An attacker can inject LDAP operators (e.g. `*)(|(cn=*`) to enumerate or bypass directory queries.

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query ('LDAP Injection')

extra.message: read() parses the partner assertion with SignedJWT.parse(text) and reads claims via getJWTClaimsSet() but never verifies the JWS signature nor a trusted key. The subject/customerRef/owningBranchCode claims are then trusted by ServiceRequestService.intakeFromPartner, so any attacker can forge a partner assertion and file requests against arbitrary customers. cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: dispatch() reads a `deliverTo` URL from the remote receiver's response body (relocationHint) and issues a follow-up POST to that attacker-controlled value (.uri(relocation)). cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: root() redirects to the unvalidated MERIDIAN_LAST_VIEW cookie value (return "redirect:" + lastView). An attacker who can set the cookie causes a redirect to an arbitrary external site (e.g. https://evil.example), an open redirect usable for phishing.

extra.message: The CORS filter reflects any request Origin into Access-Control-Allow-Origin while also setting Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true for all /api/** routes (e.g. /api/customers/typeahead returns customer data). cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: Statement pickup links are sealed with AES/CBC/PKCS5Padding using a fixed IV loaded from configuration (this.iv) and the same key for every encryption. A constant IV makes the encryption deterministic (equal statement ids produce equal ciphertext) and CBC with a reused IV leaks plaintext relationships; there is also no integrity protection.

cwe: CWE-329: Generation of Predictable IV with CBC Mode

extra.message: Password-reset tokens are generated with org.apache.commons.lang3.RandomStringUtils.randomAlphanumeric(10), which uses a non-cryptographic java.util.Random. The token is only 10 alphanumeric characters and is predictable, allowing an attacker to guess valid reset tokens.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator (PRNG)

extra.message: POST /internal/reset/initiate returns the plaintext password-reset token in its HTTP response (response.put("token", initiation.token())). Any caller able to reach this endpoint obtains a usable reset link for the named account, exposing a sensitive security credential.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: matchesStoredVerifier() accepts and compares legacy 32-hex verifiers computed with unsalted MD5 (DigestUtils.md5DigestAsHex(raw...)). MD5 is cryptographically broken and unsalted, so stored password hashes are trivially crackable; StaffAdminService also creates accounts with this same MD5 scheme.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: The break-glass operations bridge derives the presented phrase digest with MD5 (MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5")) and compares it to a configured digest. MD5 is unsuitable for protecting an authentication secret; it is fast and collision-broken, making offline brute force of the shared phrase feasible.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: The token-signing secrets used to authenticate every staff and core scope token have hardcoded default values (`staff-token-secret-demo`, `core-token-secret-demo`) baked into the shipped configuration. If the environment variable is unset, anyone can forge valid staff/core tokens and bypass authorization.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: The session cookie MERIDIAN_CONSOLE_SESSION is configured with http-only: false, so the authenticated session cookie is readable from JavaScript and can be stolen via any XSS, cookie-tossing or client-side script flaw.

cwe: CWE-1004: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag

extra.message: Spring Boot management endpoints are exposed on every interface (management.server.address: 0.0.0.0) with exposure.include: "*" (health, env, beans, heapdump, etc.). Internally reachable endpoints can leak configuration, secrets and environment data. Security misconfiguration.
